digest.component_or_area: binding_store module / peer state cluster extraction
propositions: binding_store.py at 787/800 LOC leaves only 13 lines of headroom before CI module-size gate fails the build for any contributor adding code to this file.

binding_store.py conflates two distinct concerns: binding lifecycle (bind/confirm/unbind/GC) and last-synced peer state (three-way-merge baseline and peer-parent evidence), which should be separated along an existing seam.
The last-synced peer state cluster (~130 LOC) is cohesive, has its own ADR, absence semantics, and isolated advance site in the reconciliation pass, meeting the 100-LOC floor for a standalone module.

Extraction via module-level helper functions preserves BindingStore's public surface unchanged (thin delegating methods on the store), eliminating the need to modify any existing call site or test double.

Peer state functions must be directly unit-testable without constructing a BindingStore, and absence semantics (absent baseline → local-wins, absent peer-parent → NO clear) must survive verbatim as pinned tests to prevent silent degradation during refactoring.
